title: Choose the AI that answers in {name}: free, a key or a plan
description: {name} needs an AI to write its answers. Start free with OpenRouter, use a key or a plan you already have, or a brain on this computer.
works: Every browser. A brain on this device needs a computer.
answer: {name} writes nothing by itself: an AI, which it calls a brain, writes the answers. The quickest way is free, with an OpenRouter account. You can also use a plan or a key you already have, or a brain on this computer, and change it any time in {settings} › {brains}.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {brains}, where brains are added. Next time, {settings} is in your menu at the foot of the task list.
need: To start for free, nothing: an OpenRouter account takes a minute.
For a brain on this device: a computer with about 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip, and one large download.
For a ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot plan: a computer, and one line typed in a terminal, once. {name} gives you the line on the plan’s page.
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {brains}, and press {add}.
To start for free, choose {quick}. OpenRouter’s site opens: make an account there, and you come back to {name} with a brain that answers.
To use a key you already have, choose {key}, pick its service, and paste the key you made on that service’s site.
Or choose another way: a plan you already pay for, under {paid}; a brain on this device, if it can run one; or Ollama and LM Studio, under {local}.
good: The first time, you don’t need Settings: send anything from the box, and {name} shows {first}, with the same ways.
{name} has no tie to OpenRouter, nor to any other service it offers.
OpenRouter’s free account has daily limits, and its answers come from the cloud.
A key stays on this device, encrypted. It is never in a backup.
With more than one brain, {auto} picks one for each request: quicker or stronger as the request needs, and the one on this device for anything personal.
Under every answer, {name} says which brain wrote it, and where.
fixes: The service said no to the key. See {refused}.
No brain on this device is offered
This device can’t run one: it needs about 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip. Choose a brain in the cloud instead.
Ollama or LM Studio isn’t found
They answer a browser only once they are told to, which takes a setting on your computer. If that’s more than you want, start for free with OpenRouter instead.
ask: Which brain answers me now, and how do I change it?
